name: Djibouti
summary: Lake Assal at 155 metres below sea level, whale sharks in the Gulf of Tadjoura every winter, and the Ardoukoba rift where the continent is actively splitting — all of it in a country the size of Wales.
when: November to March, when the heat is survivable and the whale sharks are in the gulf.

entries.caption: Lake Assal
entries.description: A salt lake 155 metres below sea level, ringed white, the lowest point in Africa.
entries.subject: the white salt shore and turquoise water of Lake Assal

entries.caption: The Afar Triangle
entries.description: Three tectonic plates pulling apart, and you can stand in the crack.
entries.subject: the black basalt fissures of the Ardoukoba rift

entries.caption: Whale Sharks
entries.description: They come into the Gulf of Tadjoura from November, in numbers, close to shore.
entries.subject: a whale shark swimming near the surface in the Gulf of Tadjoura

entries.caption: Day Forest
entries.description: Beira antelope and the last Djibouti francolin in the juniper of the Goda mountains.
entries.subject: juniper forest on the slopes of the Goda mountains at Day

entries.caption: The Goda and Mabla
entries.description: Mousa Ali at 2,028 metres, and juniper forest above the coastal plain at Day.
entries.subject: the Goda mountains rising above the arid coastal plain

entries.caption: Nothing Permanent
entries.description: There are no rivers here. The water is in wadis, springs and the sea.
entries.subject: a palm-shaded spring pool in a Djiboutian wadi

entries.caption: Lake Abbe
entries.description: Limestone chimneys steaming on a dry lake bed, on the Ethiopian border.
entries.subject: limestone chimneys venting steam on the flats of Lake Abbe

entries.caption: The Gulf of Tadjoura
entries.description: Beaches at Sable Blanc and the Sept Freres islands, and reef straight off the sand.
entries.subject: the white sand and clear water of Sable Blanc beach

entries.caption: The Last Juniper
entries.description: The Day forest is a relic of a wetter Horn, and it is shrinking.
entries.subject: old juniper trees in the mist of the Day forest

entries.caption: Snorkelling and Rift Walking
entries.description: Swimming with whale sharks in the morning, walking a spreading rift in the afternoon.
entries.subject: snorkellers entering the water beside a boat in the Gulf of Tadjoura

entries.caption: Afar and Somali
entries.description: Two peoples, French and Arabic official, and a port that half the Horn depends on.
entries.subject: a busy street market in Djibouti City

entries.caption: The Afar
entries.description: Salt caravans still come up from Assal, and the Afar have worked that trade for centuries.
entries.subject: an Afar man leading camels loaded with salt slabs from Lake Assal

entries.caption: Skoudehkaris and Yemeni Fish
entries.description: Spiced rice with lamb, and whole fish baked in a Yemeni clay oven on the coast.
entries.subject: a whole fish baked Yemeni-style served on flatbread

entries.caption: Independence Day
entries.description: 27 June, and the Afar and Somali dance traditions that come out for it.
entries.subject: dancers in traditional dress at a Djibouti independence celebration

entries.caption: Weaving and Woodwork
entries.description: Afar mats and milk vessels, and carved wooden headrests that double as stools.
entries.subject: a carved wooden Afar headrest and woven milk vessel

entries.caption: Ottoman Tadjoura
entries.description: One of the oldest towns on this coast, with seven mosques and a sultan's history.
entries.subject: the white mosques and low houses of Tadjoura on the gulf

entries.caption: The Lake Abbe Landscape
entries.description: Not listed, but the chimneys are on every list of the strangest places on earth.
entries.subject: steaming limestone chimneys at dawn on Lake Abbe

entries.caption: Djibouti City
entries.description: A French-Arab port city with a covered market, and the Horn's busiest container terminal.
entries.subject: the covered central market of Djibouti City

entries.caption: Arcades and Coral
entries.description: Colonial arcades in the European quarter, and coral-block houses in the old town.
entries.subject: colonnaded arcades in the European quarter of Djibouti City

entries.caption: Khat at Four
entries.description: The flight lands from Ethiopia and the city stops for it. Every afternoon.
entries.subject: men sorting bundles of khat at a street stall in the afternoon

entries.caption: Sable Blanc
entries.description: Shallow, warm, empty white sand an hour and a half from the capital.
entries.subject: a family on the empty white sand of Sable Blanc beach

entries.caption: The Ardoukoba
entries.description: A volcano that erupted in 1978 as the rift opened. The lava field is still bare.
entries.subject: the bare black lava field of the Ardoukoba volcano

entries.caption: Small and Getting Better
entries.description: A few good hotels in the capital and a diving lodge on the gulf.
entries.subject: a terrace overlooking the Gulf of Tadjoura at sunset

entries.caption: Salt, Cut by Hand
entries.description: Slabs still cut from Assal and loaded onto camels, on a route a thousand years old.
entries.subject: salt slabs being cut by hand from the crust at Lake Assal

entries.caption: White on Turquoise
entries.description: Lake Assal at midday, when the salt is blinding and the water is the wrong blue.
entries.subject: the salt crust and impossibly blue water of Lake Assal at midday

entries.caption: The Sept Freres
entries.description: Seven islands at the mouth of the gulf, with the best reef in the country round them.
entries.subject: a small boat off the Sept Freres islands with reef below

entries.caption: Why Djibouti
entries.description: Whale sharks, the lowest point in Africa and a rift valley opening, in a country you cross in a day.
entries.subject: a swimmer in clear water beside a whale shark
